newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore share market falls on bearish outlook.
newsitem.headline: Singapore share market falls on bearish outlook.

text.p: The Singapore stock market closed weaker in lethargic trade on Monday amid weariness over the island's economic prospects, dealers said.

"Interest here is relatively thin. Funds are more interested in Hong Kong and Malaysia. There is nothing bullish to look forward to in Singapore," said a dealer, adding that the weak sentiment had been manifested in undersubscribed new listings.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index ended 22.20 points down, at 2,126.66. The UOB OTC Index, which tracks Malaysian shares, was up 2.89 points at 1,191.82.
Market volume was light, at 89.7 million shares. Losers led gainers at 228 to 101.
Malaysian-linked Magnum Corp, AP Land and Antah Holdings topped the actives list with over 2.5 million shares traded in all three stocks.
Singapore Press Foreign, DBS Foreign and OCBC Foreign were among the losers, shedding between Singapore $0.60 and S$1.00.
Malaysian Technology Resources led the gainers, rising S$0.32.
